first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent it, so I sat down with the iPad and read it properly. It starts gently and says it will go in order, and there's no silly slang. The key points box near the top already mentions health care and insurance, so I knew it wasn't just pretty pictures. I kept going.

journey.section: Who keeps Albanian wedding customs today
journey.quote: They vary by region, by family and by faith, so treat what follows as a map rather than a rulebook.
journey.reaction: Good. It doesn't tell me my family's way is wrong or old-fashioned. The older ones will do it their way regardless.

journey.quote: Treat it as a courtesy to the older generation, and let them lead.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Someone finally says the grandparents should be respected rather than worked around.

journey.quote: Allow time for it in the run sheet; it is rarely quick.
journey.reaction: Practical and true. I like advice that stops the day running late.

journey.section: 10. Money gifts on the dance floor
journey.quote: A quick word with both sets of parents avoids surprises, especially with guests who have not been to an Albanian wedding before.
journey.reaction: It actually mentions the parents. That's the kind of sensible note that keeps the peace between two families.

journey.section: FAQ: Who pays for an Albanian wedding?
journey.quote: Today families split costs in their own way, so talk it through early.
journey.reaction: Fair enough, but a bit thin for the person paying. I wanted a line about getting costs and deposits agreed in writing before money changes hands.

journey.section: Travel advice for you and your guests
journey.quote: Medical facilities are limited, especially outside Tirana, and travel insurance must cover medical evacuation.
journey.reaction: This is the bit I'll forward to my husband. Honest and useful. It worries me for my mother, though, and nothing tells me how a frail guest would manage getting around or what to do if she took ill.

journey.section: Travel advice for you and your guests
journey.quote: For an outdoor wedding, note that Smartraveller warns of extreme temperatures and forest fires from April to October.
journey.reaction: Heat is a real concern for older relatives. Glad it's said plainly, but I'd want to know what you'd do about it: shade, timing, an indoor backup.

journey.section: Help from the Australian Embassy in Rome
journey.quote: Australia has no embassy or consulate in Albania, so consular help comes from the Australian Embassy in Rome.
journey.reaction: I didn't know that, and it unsettles me a little. If something goes wrong at 2am, who on your side do I actually ring? Rome is a long way away.

journey.quote: Check both with the civil status office in Albania and the Australian Embassy in Rome, including any fees.
journey.reaction: Honest that it's not settled, which I respect. But it leaves the paperwork on us. I'd hope the Advisor does this chasing.

journey.section: Travel advice for you and your guests
journey.quote: Your Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee and inclusions are agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Now that is what I want to read. One person, and the fee in writing. That's the first real reason I'd consider ringing.

unanswered_questions: Who do we ring if something goes wrong in Albania at 2am their time, given there is no Australian embassy there?
Are deposits paid to Albanian venues and suppliers protected, and who is responsible if a supplier lets us down?
Will quotes be in Australian dollars, and will contracts with Albanian suppliers be in English?
Can older guests with a walking frame manage transfers, steps and terraces at a Riviera or Tirana venue?
Does the Wedded Advisor handle the Albanian civil paperwork and translations, or is that left to us?
Can I speak with the Advisor on the phone before anything is booked?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather have one person holding the plan together, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=albanian-wedding-traditions).
turn_offs_found.why: The written fee is reassuring, but there's still nothing on deposits or who is accountable for overseas suppliers, which is my biggest fear. (Deferred business detail, not a blocker.)

would_share_with: My husband (the Smartraveller, insurance and Rome embassy sections)
My own mother and sister (the engagement, honey at the door and valle sections)

cta_reaction.quote: Your Advisor is your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee and inclusions are agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: A named contact and a written fee are exactly what I look for. I'd want to know I get a phone call first and some word on deposits and accountability overseas. More likely I'd talk to my husband and have my daughter make the first enquiry, with me on the call.

top_3_changes: Add a short checklist for older or less mobile guests in the travel section (transfers, steps, heat and shade, what insurance to confirm), as questions to check rather than invented facts.
Since consular help is in Rome, add one line near the Advisor link on who the family contacts on the ground if something goes wrong (deferred business detail, not must-fix).
In the 'Who pays' FAQ, add a practical nudge to agree each family's share and any deposits in writing early, so the paying parent feels addressed.
